description: Runs the monitor as root on Ubuntu. A local file repository serves a planted package, tctest-apt-pkg, so the result does not depend on what Ubuntu has published that day: installed at the repository's version it is healthy, and once the repository carries a newer version it alerts. A package that does not exist reports healthy (the documented 'cannot tell up to date from not installed' limit), an empty PACKAGE is refused, and a second run is harmless.

steps.label: Plant tctest-apt-pkg 1.0, installed, in a local repository
steps.run:
set -e
mkdir -p /opt/tctest-repo
# publish VERSION: build the package and rewrite the repository index (by hand: the runner has no apt-utils)
cat > /opt/tctest-publish.sh <<'EOF'
set -e
d=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$d/DEBIAN"
printf 'Package: tctest-apt-pkg\nVersion: %s\nArchitecture: all\nMaintainer: TC Test <test@example.com>\nDescription: Tier 1 test package\n' "$1" > "$d/DEBIAN/control"
dpkg-deb -b "$d" "/opt/tctest-repo/tctest-apt-pkg_$1_all.deb" >/dev/null
cd /opt/tctest-repo
for f in *.deb; do dpkg-deb -f "$f"; echo "Filename: ./$f"; echo "Size: $(stat -c %s "$f")"; echo "SHA256: $(sha256sum "$f" | cut -d ' ' -f 1)"; echo; done > Packages
# apt compares whole-second mtimes, so a republish in the same second as the last update would read as unchanged
rm -f /var/lib/apt/lists/_opt_tctest-repo_*
grep -q "^Version: $1$" Packages
EOF
bash /opt/tctest-publish.sh 1.0
dpkg -i /opt/tctest-repo/tctest-apt-pkg_1.0_all.deb >/dev/null
echo 'deb [trusted=yes] file:/opt/tctest-repo ./' > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/tctest.list
echo planted 1.0

steps.label: Publish tctest-apt-pkg 2.0 to the local repository
